children: The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2030 GMT on Wednesday:
** Investment bank Piper Sandler
and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners
have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
** Portugal's government picked Lufthansa
to buy a stake of up to 49.9% in TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) over rival Air France-KLM
, making the German airline the strategic partner of one of Europe's last unaligned flag carriers.

** The German government is in talks to acquire a 50% stake in Franco-German tank maker KNDS from its German owner families, a person close to the matter said, after conditions for an initial public offering deteriorated this year.
** France's EDF has put plans to sell a stake in its Italian subsidiary Edison
on hold due to uncertainty over gas supplies from Qatar, Edison's chief executive said, adding that the process could resume early next year.

** French businessman and former McKinsey associate Cedric Meston is taking over Duralex, the struggling glassmaker which opened administration proceedings earlier this year, said Meston and the French government. The full financial details behind the deal were not disclosed.

** Japan's top power generator JERA said it had bought the entire stake held by the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) in a Japanese consortium that holds interests in Australia's Wheatstone liquefied natural gas project. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
** Japanese trading house Sojitz

said it agreed to sell its entire stake in the Gregory Crinum coal mine in Queensland, Australia, as part of a structural reform and to reduce its exposure to metallurgical coal. The company declined to disclose the buyer or financial terms of the deal.
** Swiss skincare firm Galderma
said it had agreed to acquire US-based company ZO Skin Health for an enterprise value of $1.5 billion, confirming a report published by Reuters earlier in the day.
** Australia's New South Wales Court of Appeal rejected Cosette Pharmaceuticals' bid to terminate its takeover of Mayne Pharma
, upholding a lower court ruling that the US-based drugmaker had no valid grounds to abandon the deal.
** Australian shipbuilder Austal
said it had extended the due diligence period for Hanwha Group, allowing the South Korean conglomerate more time to formulate a formal offer for its US business, sending its shares sharply higher.
** Grupo Televisa
and Fintech Holdings have agreed to buy AT&T's
Mexican unit for $2 billion in cash, setting up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil
and marking one of Mexico's biggest M&A deals in recent years.
** The head of the Krupp Foundation, the largest shareholder in German conglomerate Thyssenkrupp
, believes there is currently a "window of opportunity" to spin off the firm's steel division, according to an interview published.
** SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc
to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies
founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million), a regulatory filing showed.
